Paragraph:
Translation: This individual soul is unbreakable and insoluble, and can be neither burned nor dried. He is everlasting, all-pervading, unchangeable, immovable and eternally the same.

Purport (Excerpt): All these qualifications of the atomic soul definitely prove that the individual soul is eternally the atomic particle of the spirit whole, and he remains the same atom eternally, without change... The word sarva-gatah (all-pervading) is significant because there is no doubt that living entities are all over God's creation.
Situation/Problem_Faced: In a world of constant chaos, loss, and instability (symbolized by the impending war), Arjuna is mentally adrift and ungrounded.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna stacks multiple adjectives of absolute stability: everlasting, unchangeable, immovable, eternally the same. He hammers home the concept of a completely static, secure core.
Outcome/Resolution: Arjuna is given a philosophical foundation of absolute permanence to counteract the chaotic impermanence of his situation.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.object Constancy (Spiritual): Knowing the self remains intact despite changes

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Krishna reiterates and solidifies the qualities of the soul, emphasizing its permanence. The soul never mutates, evolves into something else, or ceases to exist. It is structurally perfect and eternally consistent, acting as the unchanging observer across all spans of time and space.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: When experiencing extreme anxiety or panic, the mind feels like it is spinning out of control. The words used here—'unchangeable, immovable, eternally the same'—act as cognitive anchors. Repeating and internalizing these concepts provides a profound sense of grounding. It assures the individual that beneath the turbulent waves of emotion and physical threat, there is a bedrock of self that cannot be moved or altered.
